question_text:
Determine the modulus of resilience for each of the following alloys. 
      • Steel alloy:  σy = 830 MPa,  E = 207 GPa  
      • Brass alloy:  σy = 380 MPa,  E = 97 GPa  
      • Aluminum alloy:  σy = 275 MPa,  E = 69 GPa  
      • Titanium alloy:  σy = 690 MPa,  E = 107 GPa  

Give your answer as a tuple (modulus of resilience for Steel alloy, Brass alloy, Aluminum alloy, Titanium alloy).

Reference:
"Table 7.1 Room-Temperature Elastic and Shear Moduli and Poisson's Ratio for Various Materials

\hline Aluminum & 69 & 10 & 25 & 3.6 & 0.33 \\

\hline \multicolumn{6}{|c|}{Ceramic Materials} \\
\hline Aluminum oxide ( $\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ ) & 393 & 57 & - & - & 0.22 \\

\hline Glass-ceramic (Pyroceram) & 120 & 17 & - & - & 0.25 \\

\hline Phenol-formaldehyde & 2.76-4.83 & 0.40-0.70 & - & - & - \\

${ }^b$ Modern Plastics Encyclopedia '96, McGraw-Hill, New York, 1995."The units of each required answer are (J/m^3, J/m^3, J/m^3, J/m^3), respectively.
response:
The modulus of resilience is the strain energy per unit volume absorbed up to the yield point:

$$U_r = \frac{\sigma_y^2}{2E}$$

Computing each (converting E to MPa so the result is in MJ/m³ = 10⁶ J/m³):

- **Steel:** 830²/(2·207000) = 1.664 × 10⁶ J/m³
- **Brass:** 380²/(2·97000) = 0.744 × 10⁶ J/m³
- **Aluminum:** 275²/(2·69000) = 0.548 × 10⁶ J/m³
- **Titanium:** 690²/(2·107000) = 2.224 × 10⁶ J/m³

$$\boxed{(1.66\times10^{6},\ 0.74\times10^{6},\ 0.55\times10^{6},\ 2.22\times10^{6})}$$
